title: Given a `List<Employee>`, build one comma-separated string of all their names using the stream `reduce()` operation (not `Collectors.joining`).
shortTitle: Concatenate all employee names into a single string separated by ", " using reduce()

s1_definition.profdef: You first `map` each Employee to its name, producing a `Stream<String>`, then fold the names into one string. The three-argument `reduce("", (partial, name) -> ..., (s1, s2) -> ...)` starts from an empty string and appends each name with a ", " separator, taking care not to prepend a separator before the very first name.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya is writing one line listing everyone on the team: "Rajesh, Priya, Amit". She starts with an empty line, adds the first name, and for each later name adds a comma-space and then the name. That "start empty and keep appending with a separator" is exactly what reduce does here.
s1_definition.oneliner: reduce from "" and append each name, inserting ", " only when the running string is not empty.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** You first `map` each Employee to its name, producing a `Stream<String>`, then fold the names into one string. The three-argument `reduce("", (partial, name) -> ..., (s1, s2) -> ...)` starts from an empty string and appends each name with a ", " separator, taking care not to prepend a separator before the very first name.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Priya is writing one line listing everyone on the team: "Rajesh, Priya, Amit". She starts with an empty line, adds the first name, and for each later name adds a comma-space and then the name. That "start empty and keep appending with a separator" is exactly what reduce does here.

**One line to remember:** reduce from "" and append each name, inserting ", " only when the running string is not empty.

sections.s2_technical:
After `map(Employee::getName)` the stream holds strings. The fold identity is the empty string `""`. The accumulator appends: if the running string is empty we just use the name, otherwise we use `running + ", " + name`. This avoids a leading comma before the first name. For example the sequence folds "" then "Rajesh" then "Rajesh, Priya" then "Rajesh, Priya, Amit".

The combiner for parallel execution must also join two non-empty partial strings with ", ". A correct combiner is `(s1, s2) -> s1.isEmpty() ? s2 : (s2.isEmpty() ? s1 : s1 + ", " + s2)`. This keeps the result correct whether the stream is sequential or parallel.

A senior point about performance: repeated `String` concatenation in a reduce creates many intermediate String objects, which is O(n squared) in the worst case. For production I would use `Collectors.joining(", ")`, which internally uses a `StringBuilder` and is far more efficient and simpler. The question asks for `reduce` specifically to show the folding mechanics, so I implement it that way while naming the better tool.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — The National Bank of India emails a team roster and needs the member names on one line, comma-separated, with no stray leading comma. Building that string by naive concatenation often produces ", Rajesh, Priya". This is exactly the problem the empty-check in the reduce accumulator solves.

Problem 2 — The roster code might run in parallel over a large list, so the join must still be correct. This is exactly why the combiner must also join two partial strings with the separator.

The code defines `Employee`, a `RosterService` with `joinNames`, and a runnable demo.

sections.s5_journey:
Input names after map: "Rajesh", "Priya", "Amit".

Step 1: Identity is "".

Step 2: Accumulator with "" and "Rajesh": running is empty, so result is "Rajesh".

Step 3: With "Rajesh" and "Priya": running is non-empty, so result is "Rajesh, Priya".

Step 4: With "Rajesh, Priya" and "Amit": result is "Rajesh, Priya, Amit".

Step 5: The final string is returned, with no leading comma.

```
INFO: Team roster: Rajesh, Priya, Amit
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  Input: [Employee(Rajesh), Employee(Priya), Employee(Amit)]
    │ map(Employee::getName)
    ▼
  Stream<String>: "Rajesh","Priya","Amit"
    │ reduce("", append-with-separator, combiner)
    │
    │ ""                          (identity)
    ├─ + "Rajesh"  → "Rajesh"     (empty → no comma)
    ├─ + "Priya"   → "Rajesh, Priya"
    └─ + "Amit"    → "Rajesh, Priya, Amit"
    ▼
  Output: "Rajesh, Priya, Amit"
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
To concatenate names with reduce I first map each employee to its name so the stream holds strings, then fold them starting from an empty string. The accumulator is careful: if the running string is empty it just takes the name, otherwise it appends ", " and then the name. That empty-check is what prevents a stray leading comma before the first name, which is the classic bug in a naive join.

Because the stream could run in parallel I also supply a combiner that joins two partial strings with the same ", " separator and handles the case where either side is empty, so the result is correct sequentially and in parallel.

In my banking project at the National Bank of India this built a one-line, comma-separated team roster for a notification email. The senior point I always add is that repeated String concatenation in a reduce creates many intermediate String objects and can be quadratic, so in real code I would use `Collectors.joining(", ")`, which uses a StringBuilder internally and is both simpler and far more efficient. I implement it with reduce here specifically to demonstrate that I understand the folding mechanics underneath joining.

---

keyPoints: reduce(): combines all elements into single result
Two forms: reduce(identity, accumulator) and reduce(accumulator)
identity is the starting value (0 for sum, empty string for concat)
